subject: Errors when trying to run Nimble in parallel using foreach

messages.author: 46f76d1903dc6874
messages.subject: Errors when trying to run Nimble in parallel using foreach
parts:
I'm getting this strange error when trying to run multiple models (not chains) in parallel with nimble using foreach and DoParallel:


Error in { : 
  task 2 failed - "C symbol name "new_lifted_chol_oPbeta_hurdle_cov_oB1to2_comma_1to2_cB_cP_L9_UID_8" not in load table"


The pertinent code in the function that I'm running in parallel is:

  output <- nimbleMCMC(code = model,
                       constants = nimble_consts,
                       data = nimble_data,
                       inits = nimble_inits,
                       nchains = 3,
                       monitors = c("beta_abundance", 
                                    "beta_hurdle",
                                    "r"),
                       niter = n_iter + n_burnin,
                       nburnin = n_burnin,
                       WAIC = TRUE)

where nimble_* objects vary for each job. Everything works as expected when run outside of foreach in serial.

I do all model, function, data, etc., definition separately on each worker, and I'm using a FORK cluster. Any guidance or hypotheses about what might be going on? I can provide a minimum working example but it will take a while, I just wanted to post this error message to get things started and see if it might be something obvious.

Thanks!
Vincent

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Errors when trying to run Nimble in parallel using foreach
parts:
hi Vincent,

Parallelization with NIMBLE is a bit tricky (we have plans to improve this in the long-term) because of how our C++ objects are managed from within R. We have an example on our webpage that discusses this and shows how to do things. Can you take a look at that and let us know if modifying what you are doing based on that doesn't work?

https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/parallelizing_NIMBLE.html

In particular, you can't use a fork cluster. If you have been using a fork cluster it would be surprising if it ever worked.

-Chris
